# Results — Study 94 (Level-Pegging) on the real total-return tapes

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — hold the
**equal-weight S&P (RSP)** vs the **cap-weight S&P (SPY)**, total return, buy-and-hold both,
net each arm of its fee (RSP **20 bps/yr**, SPY **9 bps/yr**), and read the race full-sample
and across the mega-cap-leadership split at **2015-01-01**. As-of **2026-06-12**; match the
fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tapes. Window is **RSP-bounded from 2003** — there is
no investable equal-weight S&P tape before RSP's 2003 inception.*

## Data stamp

| Series | Window | Rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| RSP (equal-weight) + SPY (cap-weight), total return | 2003-05-01 → 2026-06-12 | 5,817 | `5d3261d7897c` |

## The full-sample race — GROSS (total return, no fees)

| Arm | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe | Max drawdown | Growth of $1 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| RSP equal-weight | 11.29% | 19.8% | 0.640 | −59.9% | 11.82× |
| SPY cap-weight | **11.49%** | 18.5% | **0.679** | **−55.2%** | **12.31×** |

Even **gross of fees**, equal-weight does *not* beat cap-weight over the full RSP era: it
trails by **0.20 pts/yr** of CAGR, carries more volatility and a deeper drawdown, and ends
with **less** wealth. Net of fees the gap widens.

## The full-sample race — NET (RSP −20 bps/yr, SPY −9 bps/yr)

| Arm | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe | Max drawdown | Growth of $1 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| RSP equal-weight | 11.07% | 19.8% | 0.630 | −60.1% | 11.29× |
| SPY cap-weight | **11.39%** | 18.5% | **0.675** | **−55.2%** | **12.05×** |

## The decisive numbers

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| EW − CW CAGR gap, full sample (net) | **−0.32 pts/yr** (EW *loses*) |
| HAC *t* on the daily EW−CW return difference (net) | **−0.04** (indistinguishable from zero) |
| Block-bootstrap 95% CI, mean daily diff | **[−0.90, +0.85] bps/day** (straddles 0) |
| EW-on-CW alpha (annualised, full sample) | **−0.23%/yr**, HAC *t* = **−0.21**, β = **1.02**, R² = **0.92** |
| RSP/SPY relative wealth | peaked at **1.305** on **2011-05-20**, now **0.936** |

## The regime split — where the whole story lives

| Sub-period | EW − CW (annualised) | HAC *t* | Winner |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| **Early 2003-05 → 2015-01** (broadening) | **+2.60%/yr** | +1.97 | **EW** |
| **Late 2015-01 → 2026-06** (mega-cap led) | **−2.74%/yr** | −1.57 | **CW** |
| **Difference-of-differences** | **+5.34 pts/yr** | — | — |

The two sub-periods are genuinely different, not eyeballed: a **circular block bootstrap**
(5,000 resamples, 21-day blocks, re-split at the same calendar fraction) on the
difference-of-differences gives **p = 0.0188**. Early-era Sharpe favoured EW (0.622 vs 0.552);
late-era Sharpe favours CW decisively (0.644 vs 0.814).

## How to read it

- **"Always beats" is false.** Equal-weight *led* through the broadening 2003-2011 market
  (RSP/SPY relative wealth peaked at 1.305 in 2011) and *lagged* badly through the mega-cap
  run that followed — relative wealth fell to 0.936, i.e. RSP has *underperformed* SPY over the
  full investable history. → 3rd axis **BUSTED**.
- **The full-sample edge is not just thin — it's the wrong sign and not robust.** CAGR gap
  −0.32 pts/yr net, HAC *t* on the difference ≈ 0, alpha −0.23%/yr with *t* = −0.21 and a beta
  of ~1.02 (EW is essentially the same market with a small-cap/anti-concentration tilt, R²
  0.92). → Signal **WEAK / MIXED** (regime-split: real-ish edge early, gone-to-negative late).
- **As an "always" trade it's a MIRAGE; as a regime bet it's real but conditional.** The tilt
  pays when breadth widens and loses when it narrows; you have to *time the regime*, which the
  claim explicitly tells you not to do. → Tradability **MIRAGE** for the "just buy RSP" claim.

## Reproduce

```bash
python examples/verify.py              # real tape (this doc)
python examples/run_synthetic_demo.py  # offline positive/negative control
```
